answer: Agents register a hardware-rooted, time-varying fingerprint derived from on-chip ring-oscillator jitter; each epoch they publish a zk-SNARK proving the fingerprint matches the previous epoch's commitment, and the network verifies the proof against a public onyx-seeded randomness beacon. An attacker must reproduce the exact analog noise of each device, which costs at least the silicon area of the original chip plus the echo of the beacon's entropy, making mass-scale sybil creation economically equivalent to fabricating new shale-grade ASICs.
